what_this_is_not: R values are copied from the tracked fixture. Julia values are computed fresh by tools/true_parity_cov_ord_latent_receipt.jl, which repeats the computation of the cited twin test with the same inputs and settings; R was not run and is not recomputed here.

cases.julia_source: fit.loglik, as compared at test/test_cov_ord_latent_p1.jl:102; fit as at test/test_cov_ord_latent_p1.jl:94
cases.note: Gaussian fit of value ~ 0 + trait + latent(0 + trait | site, common = TRUE): Sigma_B = L L' + psi I_p (R's common unique diagonal, one theta_diag_B), residual SD fixed by R at max(0.001 sd(y), 1e-6), unit = site, on one simulated data set (n = 60 sites, p = 4 traits, one observation per trait and site; data CSV sha256 checked; R fitted the data read back from that CSV). R converged (nlminb code 0, rel.tol / sing.tol / x.tol 1e-12, max |gradient| 3.8e-5) with a positive-definite Hessian; R's logLik df = 9 = Julia's free-parameter count. Julia fits the same covariance, I_n kron Sigma_B + sigma_eps^2 I, as fit_gaussian_sources with SourceCovariance(I_n; mode = :latent, rank = 1, unique = true, common = true) (source at test/test_cov_ord_latent_p1.jl:93), g_tol 1e-8, sigma_eps_fixed = R's fixed value. Model identity is checked directly: the Julia objective at R's optimum and at R's perturbed probe point (opt$par + 0.05 sin(1:k), R's -obj$fn there) reproduces R's value. Limits: Gaussian only; rank 1; one observation per site and trait; the Julia side is the native source fitter, not formula sugar for latent().
